question: Which service is a key part of disease prevention in comprehensive health care?

options.A: Performing major open-heart surgeries
options.B: Giving routine immunizations to children
options.C: Importing expensive specialized drugs
options.D: Building high-rise luxury hospitals

explanation: Immunizations stop preventable infectious diseases from spreading through a community, making them a core preventive service. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h3)

question: When is a doctor most likely to order a liver biopsy?

options.A: For routine check-ups on healthy students
options.B: To check how well the kidneys are filtering waste
options.C: When blood tests and scans don't explain strange liver results
options.D: When a patient is just feeling tired and slightly dehydrated

explanation: You got it! When basic tests like blood work and ultrasounds leave doctors guessing, a biopsy helps give a clear, definitive answer. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T10#GNS221_U2_T10_h1)

question: What is the correct order of assessment techniques for most body parts?

options.A: Percussion, auscultation, palpation, inspection
options.B: Palpation, inspection, auscultation, percussion
options.C: Inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation
options.D: Auscultation, percussion, inspection, palpation

explanation: For most body systems, you look first, feel second, tap third, and listen last. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which body posture helps open up the spaces between the vertebrae for a spinal tap?

options.A: Arching the back backward with arms extended
options.B: Lying completely flat on the back with straight legs
options.C: Sitting upright with shoulders pulled straight back
options.D: Curled up with knees and chin tucked inward

explanation: Spot on! Flexing the spine forward separates the bones, widening the gap so the needle can pass through easily. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h5)

question: When should you, as the nurse, do your final dosage calculation?

options.A: Only when the pharmacist calls
options.B: Right before giving the drug
options.C: After a bad reaction happens
options.D: During your annual nursing review

explanation: Always double-check your math right before administration. It is your last chance to catch mistakes before the drug enters the patient's body. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h1)

question: A nursing mother complains of painful swelling and redness in only her left calf. What should you do?

options.A: Advise her to apply hot compresses and stay in bed for three days
options.B: Prescribe oral iron supplements for suspected postpartum anaemia
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal muscular strain from carrying the baby
options.D: Refer her urgently for suspected deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Pain and swelling in just one leg is a warning sign of a blood clot (DVT). It needs an urgent hospital check to keep her safe! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T022#GNS226_U3_T022_h2)

question: Which hormone is produced by the Leydig cells in the testes?

options.A: Testosterone
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Great job! The Leydig cells are responsible for making testosterone, which is the main male sex hormone. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to prescribe antibiotics along with draining an abscess?

options.A: The presence of severe surrounding skin redness and swelling
options.B: The patient developing a fever and systemic chills
options.C: The patient simply prefers taking pills over wound care
options.D: The patient having a compromised immune system

explanation: Antibiotics are powerful drugs reserved for spreading infections, fevers, or weak immune systems—never just because a patient prefers taking pills over doing proper wound care. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T4#GNS311_U4_T4_h6)

question: What key tip should you teach a mother giving an oral suspension to her toddler at home?

options.A: Store the open bottle on a sunny kitchen windowsill
options.B: Shake the bottle well immediately before every single dose
options.C: Mix the entire bottle with juice and keep it on the counter
options.D: Stop the medication as soon as the child feels better

explanation: Empowering mothers with good education is key! Reminding them to shake the bottle every time ensures the child gets the exact medicine they need. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h6)

question: Why must a nurse catch postpartum infections early?

options.A: Postpartum infections can quickly escalate into systemic illness and shock
options.B: It guarantees the patient will not need any form of surgical intervention
options.C: Delayed involution of the uterus is the only complication that ever occurs
options.D: Routine hospital discharge protocols require a confirmed negative blood culture

explanation: Spotting an infection early makes a huge difference! A localized postpartum infection can quickly turn into severe sepsis if we don't catch and treat it promptly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h1)

question: What is the main difference between shear and friction in skin breakdown?

options.A: Shear only happens on the heels, whereas friction only happens on the sacrum.
options.B: Shear happens when bones slide inside while skin stays stuck; friction is just surface rubbing.
options.C: Shear damages bone tissue, whereas friction only damages hair follicles.
options.D: Shear is caused by moisture, whereas friction is caused by lack of protein.

explanation: Friction is like skin rubbing against bedsheets, but shear happens when the skeleton slides down while the outer skin stays put, twisting the blood vessels inside. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why must internal transport routes avoid patient dining areas and crowded waiting rooms?

options.A: To minimize the risk of accidental exposure and public anxiety
options.B: To prevent the waste from cooling down too quickly
options.C: To ensure the waste carts move at a faster speed
options.D: To comply with architectural design rules for elevators

explanation: Moving hazardous waste through clean, crowded public spaces creates unnecessary infection risks and alarms patients. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: Which action best demonstrates a nurse acting to promote wellness?

options.A: Teaching a community group about balanced diets and regular exercise
options.B: Discharging a patient without giving any instructions on home care
options.C: Refusing to answer questions about a patient's prescribed diet
options.D: Waiting until a chronic disease becomes terminal before intervening

explanation: Health education and lifestyle promotion are core nursing interventions for wellness. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why do sprained ligaments usually take a long time to heal?

options.A: Ligaments are constantly exposed to air
options.B: Ligaments lack any nerve endings to signal repair
options.C: Ligaments have a poor direct blood supply
options.D: Ligaments are made of bone tissue which cannot regenerate

explanation: Spot on! Ligaments have very few blood vessels running through them, meaning healing nutrients take much longer to arrive. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h8)

question: What does male sexual dysfunction mainly affect?

options.A: Upper respiratory function
options.B: Physical intimacy and satisfaction
options.C: Renal filtration capacity
options.D: Skeletal muscle development

explanation: You've got this! Male sexual dysfunction simply means there's trouble with enjoying or engaging in sexual activity. It's all about intimacy and satisfaction. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T24#GNS312_U1_T24_h1)

question: Why is teaching a practical skill alone often not enough for economic empowerment?

options.A: Most skills taught in centers are already outdated within one month.
options.B: Government laws forbid disabled individuals from owning private businesses.
options.C: Skills training causes physical fatigue that worsens disability.
options.D: Trainees also need startup capital, equipment, and market access to succeed.

explanation: Learning a trade is brilliant, but without the right tools and a way to sell their goods or services, graduates will still struggle to generate income. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h4)

question: Where do the bones of your skull and jaw mostly come from during early development?

options.A: Visceral endoderm
options.B: Neural crest cells
options.C: Pelvic mesoderm
options.D: Cardiac jelly

explanation: Think of neural crest cells as great travelers—they migrate forward into the head region early on to form your face and skull bones! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T1#GNS121_U3_T1_h1)

question: What important detail must be included when charting medication drop administration?

options.A: The brand name of the box the bottle came in
options.B: The room temperature during the procedure
options.C: The exact weight of the glass dropper bottle
options.D: The specific eye, ear, or nostril treated

explanation: Recording the exact side and site ensures continuity of care and prevents treating the wrong side later. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h9)

question: How does your blood protect your body against germs and infections?

options.A: By increasing the total volume of red blood cells
options.B: By filtering toxins directly through the skin
options.C: By lowering blood pressure during an illness
options.D: By circulating white blood cells and antibodies

explanation: Exactly! Your bloodstream acts like a highway, rushing white blood cells and antibodies straight to wherever germs are trying to attack. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T1#GNS311_U2_T1_h2)

question: How do secondary causes differ from primary causes of nephrotic conditions?

options.A: Secondary causes always resolve completely without medication
options.B: Secondary causes only affect adults over the age of sixty
options.C: Primary causes involve infections outside the urinary tract
options.D: Secondary causes are systemic diseases that damage the kidneys as a complication

explanation: You're doing great! Think of primary causes as starting right in the kidney, while secondary causes happen when a whole-body condition like diabetes or lupus ends up hurting the kidneys along the way. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which part of the early blastocyst grows to become the baby's side of the placenta?

options.A: Amniotic cavity
options.B: Zona pellucida
options.C: Trophoblast
options.D: Inner cell mass

explanation: You've got this! The outer layer, called the trophoblast, reaches out to connect with the mother's uterine lining to form the placenta. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T4#GNS121_U6_T4_h1)

question: What is the typical acid-base blood gas state during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Acute metabolic alkalosis
options.B: Uncompensated metabolic acidosis
options.C: Severe respiratory acidosis
options.D: Compensated respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Mums breathe off extra carbon dioxide, leading to mild respiratory alkalosis which the kidneys smoothly balance out with bicarbonate. Great revision! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T3#GNS121_U7_T3_h4)

question: When is a doctor or lab scientist most likely to order a peripheral blood smear along with a regular full blood count?

options.A: As a quick kidney check before surgery
options.B: To check how much iron the patient eats over time
options.C: When the standard blood count shows unexpected results
options.D: To replace measuring total haemoglobin

explanation: A blood smear lets the lab actually look at the cells under a microscope when the numbers on the regular blood test look a bit strange. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness?

options.A: To ensure the mother pays all hospital bills in advance
options.B: To completely eliminate any need for hospital visits
options.C: To reduce delays in getting emergency care during childbirth
options.D: To guarantee that the baby is born on a specific weekday

explanation: Correct! Planning ahead with transport and funds stops dangerous delays when things get critical during labor. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h7)

question: A patient arrives at the ward struggling to breathe with swollen legs from heart failure. Which drug type is best to give right away for quick relief?

options.A: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor
options.B: Potassium-sparing diuretic
options.C: Loop diuretic
options.D: Osmotic diuretic

explanation: When you need fast, powerful fluid removal in an emergency like severe swelling or breathing trouble, loop diuretics are your go-to choice! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h3)

question: How is a Stage 1 pressure sore best identified on light-skinned patients?

options.A: Intact skin with redness that does not turn white when pressed
options.B: An open crater exposing subcutaneous fat and muscle
options.C: A black, hard scab covering deep tissue damage
options.D: A shallow pink wound with clear fluid drainage

explanation: In Stage 1, the skin isn't broken yet, but it shows redness that stays red even when you press a finger on it (non-blanching). Good to know for your ward rotations! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the main difference between vehicle-borne and vector-borne transmission?

options.A: Vehicle transmission is restricted strictly to airborne droplet nuclei.
options.B: Vehicle transmission requires direct physical contact between humans.
options.C: Vector transmission only occurs through contaminated food and water supplies.
options.D: Vehicle transmission involves non-living objects, while vector transmission involves living organisms.

explanation: Spot on! Vehicles are non-living things like water or food, while vectors are living creatures like insects. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T13#GNS313_U1_T13_h3)

question: What is the medical term for difficult or abnormal labour?

options.A: Eutocia
options.B: Inversion
options.C: Placenta praevia
options.D: Dystocia

explanation: Great job! Dystocia simply means labour isn't progressing smoothly. Think of 'eu-' as normal and 'dys-' as difficult. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T003#GNS226_U3_T003_h1)

question: Which member of the healthcare team is a medical doctor who specializes in physical medicine and rehab?

options.A: Social worker
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: A physiatrist is a doctor who leads the medical side of physical medicine and rehabilitation. Great job keeping terms straight! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h2)

question: What is the main reason a nurse gives an intradermal injection (just under the top layer of skin)?

options.A: Delivering rapid pain relief during acute trauma.
options.B: Providing daily maintenance doses of intravenous fluids.
options.C: Vaccinating large populations against seasonal influenza.
options.D: Diagnostic testing like allergy or tuberculosis screenings.

explanation: Spot on! Because skin layers absorb very slowly here, it's the perfect spot to watch for a localized immune reaction like a TB test. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h4)

question: Why must you know the anatomy of the vulva well before taking a sample?

options.A: To determine the exact hormonal cycle day of the patient accurately
options.B: To calculate the correct dosage of antibiotics needed for treatment
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling any discomfort during the procedure
options.D: To ensure the sample is collected from the exact symptomatic area

explanation: Knowing your landmarks—like the labia and clitoris—helps you swab the exact spot where the sore or discharge is, ensuring accurate lab results! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h1)

question: Peptic ulcer treatment usually focuses on balancing which two opposing forces in the stomach?

options.A: Red blood cell counts and white blood cell counts
options.B: Dietary sugar intake and physical exercise levels
options.C: Fluid intake and urinary output volume
options.D: Aggressive acid factors and defensive mucosal factors

explanation: Think of it as a tug-of-war! Strong acid tries to damage the stomach, while the stomach's natural mucus tries to protect it. Drugs help restore that balance. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary job of ligaments in our joints?

options.A: To connect skeletal muscle directly to bone
options.B: To cushion the ends of bones from friction
options.C: To connect bone to bone and provide stability
options.D: To produce lubricating synovial fluid

explanation: Spot on! Ligaments are tough bands of tissue holding bones together so your joints stay stable when you move or carry weight. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h4)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a sore on her labia that hasn't healed in four months. What should you suspect?

options.A: A normal hormonal change related to approaching menopause
options.B: A simple Bartholin gland cyst that will resolve on its own
options.C: A potential malignant vulval lesion requiring a biopsy
options.D: An acute yeast infection that needs oral antifungal medication

explanation: Spot on! Any sore or ulcer down there that refuses to heal after weeks must be checked for cancer through a biopsy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h4)

question: You feel an organ extending past the left rib margin during a deep abdominal exam. What organ are you most likely feeling?

options.A: Kidney
options.B: Liver
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Spleen

explanation: The spleen hangs out in the upper left side of the abdomen. If it's enlarged, it extends downward from beneath the left ribs where you can feel it. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T3#GNS311_U2_T3_h6)

question: In nursing, what does the term 'medication adherence' actually mean?

options.A: The speed at which a drug dissolves in the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: The extent to which a patient takes their medication as agreed with providers
options.C: The chemical binding force holding tablet ingredients together
options.D: The physical strength of the plastic bottle cap protecting the pills

explanation: Adherence is just a teamwork word for whether the patient is taking their drugs the way you both agreed on. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why are day care centres considered important community health resources?

options.A: They offer permanent housing for abandoned elderly individuals
options.B: They provide safe supervision and social support while caregivers work
options.C: They serve as boarding schools for school-aged adolescents
options.D: They replace the need for primary healthcare clinics entirely

explanation: These centres support families by caring for dependents safely during working hours, promoting both child development and adult well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical reason why patients struggle to sleep in a hospital?

options.A: Comfortable room temperatures and soft lighting
options.B: Physical pain and post-operative discomfort
options.C: Frequent nighttime vital sign checks by staff
options.D: Constant noise from equipment and hallway chatter

explanation: Hospitals are usually noisy, bright, and busy with checks—not exactly a peaceful spa! Comfortable conditions actually help patients sleep. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T9#GNS112_U4_T9_h3)

question: What is the main job of a bronchodilator in the airways?

options.A: Dissolving thick mucus plugs inside the bronchioles
options.B: Stopping the immune system from causing inflammation
options.C: Reducing bacterial infections in lung tissue
options.D: Relaxing bronchial smooth muscle to widen the airway

explanation: Bronchodilators help you breathe easier by relaxing the tight muscles around your airways, making them wider for air to pass through. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why do some families prefer having FGM done by a healthcare worker instead of a traditional cutter?

options.A: Hospitals provide free reconstructive surgery
options.B: Traditional practitioners charge higher fees
options.C: They believe clinical settings make the procedure safe
options.D: The government mandates clinical procedures

explanation: Many families think that because it's done in a clinic with clean tools and pain relief, the harmful risks disappear. But medicalised FGM is still dangerous and harmful! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h1)

question: What is the main goal of sperm capacitation?

options.A: To slow down the swimming speed of the sperm
options.B: To increase the total number of chromosomes in the sperm head
options.C: To prepare the sperm membrane and enhance its ability to fertilize the oocyte
options.D: To help the sperm attach securely to the vaginal wall

explanation: Spot on! Capacitation is basically the maturation process inside the female tract that gets the sperm ready to do the job. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T8#GNS121_U5_T8_h3)

question: Why must you be careful when looking at a trend on a scatter diagram?

options.A: Graphs can only show data from fewer than ten patients
options.B: Correlation does not automatically prove cause and effect
options.C: Numbers on the axes change every time the page is refreshed
options.D: Visual plots cannot be used for clinical decision making

explanation: Just because two things move together on a graph doesn't mean one directly caused the other. Always keep your critical thinking cap on! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T12#GNS217_U4_T12_h2)

question: Why is the epiglottis such an important little flap in your throat?

options.A: It separates the nasal cavity from the oral cavity
options.B: It regulates the speed of airflow into the lungs during exercise
options.C: It prevents food and liquid from entering the trachea during swallowing
options.D: It produces mucus to trap dust particles in the nasal passages

explanation: You got it! The epiglottis acts like a clever trapdoor, closing over your windpipe when you swallow so food goes safely down your food pipe instead. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the main focus of an adult day care centre?

options.A: Offering specialized infant feeding and sleeping routines
options.B: Preparing young children for primary school entry
options.C: Conducting major surgeries for elderly patients
options.D: Providing companionship and medication management

explanation: Adult day care centres focus on keeping elderly or disabled clients safe, socially engaged, and compliant with their daily medications. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why are older adults at a higher risk of becoming dehydrated?

options.A: Their kidneys retain excess water automatically
options.B: They experience a blunted thirst response
options.C: They have an increased sense of thirst
options.D: Their body mass contains more water than younger adults

explanation: Older adults often don't feel thirsty even when their bodies are low on water because their natural thirst signals get weaker with age. Always encourage fluids! [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h6)

question: What does 'event-related sterility' mean for packaged instruments sitting in storage?

options.A: Sterility depends entirely on the specific time of day it was processed
options.B: Instruments lose their sterility the moment they are placed on a shelf
options.C: All items automatically expire exactly seven days after autoclaving
options.D: Items remain sterile until the packaging is damaged or exposed to moisture

explanation: Instead of worrying about a strict calendar expiration date, packs stay sterile as long as the packaging remains safe and dry! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)

question: What physical characteristic indicates that a vein is a poor choice for cannulation?

options.A: The vein bounces back softly when pressed
options.B: The vein is clearly visible under light skin
options.C: The vein feels hard, rigid, and cord-like
options.D: The vein disappears temporarily when warmed

explanation: Hard or sclerosed veins are damaged and fragile, meaning they will easily rupture or fail to hold a cannula. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h4)

question: How does Root Cause Analysis differ from traditional blame-oriented approaches?

options.A: RCA takes place before the patient even enters the hospital.
options.B: RCA focuses on fixing broken systems instead of blaming individuals.
options.C: RCA ignores human mistakes completely and focuses only on finance.
options.D: RCA is performed solely by patients rather than healthcare staff.

explanation: Modern patient safety principles recognize that human error is usually a symptom of deeper, faulty system designs. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h4)

question: A newly intubated patient is on a ventilator. You notice the left side of the chest is barely moving and you cannot hear breath sounds there. What likely happened?

options.A: The ventilator settings have too much positive end-expiratory pressure
options.B: The tube has slipped into the right mainstem bronchus
options.C: The oxygen source has become disconnected from the machine
options.D: The patient is developing a severe tension pneumothorax

explanation: The right breathing pipe (bronchus) is a straight shot down, so tubes often slide too far in and end up ventilating only the right lung, leaving the left side quiet. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T10#GNS321_U2_T10_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of analyzing epidemiologic data?

options.A: To turn raw numbers into understandable patterns of health
options.B: To replace the need for physical patient examinations
options.C: To make collection forms look neat and professional
options.D: To hide mistakes made during community surveys

explanation: Analysis organizes scattered information so nurses can see where and why health issues are occurring. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which type of injury happens at the exact moment a physical blow or crash occurs?

options.A: Metabolic injury
options.B: Primary injury
options.C: Tertiary injury
options.D: Secondary injury

explanation: That's correct! The primary injury is the immediate damage that happens right at the time of impact, like torn tissue or bruising. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h2)

question: Which official body holds Nigerian nurses legally accountable for their practice?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: West African Health Organization
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: That's our umbrella body! The NMCN regulates nursing education and practice in Nigeria, keeping our profession standard and legal. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h2)

question: Why is female genital mutilation (FGM) traditionally performed?

options.A: To prevent severe pelvic infections in young girls
options.B: To enhance natural hormonal balance during puberty
options.C: To treat congenital reproductive disorders
options.D: To comply with non-medical cultural and social beliefs

explanation: Spot on! FGM is done for cultural or social reasons, not for any medical treatment or health benefit. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary role of glucagon during a fasting state?

options.A: To signal the liver to release stored glucose into the blood
options.B: To help the pancreas produce more beta cells for energy
options.C: To block insulin from entering the muscle tissues
options.D: To transport excess sugar directly to the kidneys for excretion

explanation: When fasting lowers blood sugar, glucagon tells the liver to break down stored glycogen to keep blood sugar from dropping too low. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the chemical neurotransmitter released at the neuromuscular junction?

options.A: Serotonin
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Norepinephrine

explanation: Acetylcholine is released from motor neurons to cross the synapse and stimulate muscle fiber membranes. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is the main idea behind restorative nursing care for elderly patients?

options.A: To replace physical therapy sessions entirely
options.B: To diagnose new chronic illnesses in older adults
options.C: To provide heavy sedation during painful medical procedures
options.D: To integrate rehabilitation principles into daily nursing routines

explanation: Exactly! Restorative nursing simply means weaving rehab into everyday actions like bathing, eating, and getting out of bed. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h3)

question: A patient arrives with a deep dog puncture on their hand. After checking the ABCs, what should the nurse assess first?

options.A: The patient's current insurance and employment details
options.B: Distal pulses, motor function, and finger sensation
options.C: Whether the patient prefers oral or intravenous medication
options.D: The exact monetary value of any damaged clothing

explanation: Always check circulation, movement, and feeling early on! Deep punctures can easily cause hidden damage to nearby blood vessels and tendons. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h3)

question: In midwifery, what is the medical term for a normal, uncomplicated vaginal delivery?

options.A: Dystocia
options.B: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.C: Placenta praevia
options.D: Eutocia

explanation: You'll often hear 'eutocia' used to describe a smooth, straightforward birth with no major hitches. It's the exact opposite of dystocia! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h1)

question: A ward manager notices more patient falls happening. What should they do right after gathering this data?

options.A: Write a brand new job description for the ward clerk
options.B: Ignore the data until the end of the fiscal year audit
options.C: Compare the fall rates against the established hospital safety benchmark
options.D: Immediately fire the nurses working the night shift without investigation

explanation: Once you collect the data, the logical next step is to compare it to your hospital's safety standard to see how big the gap is. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h2)

question: A new nurse is sorting waste on a busy ward. Which action shows they are following safety rules correctly?

options.A: Dropping a used syringe directly into a puncture-resistant box without recapping
options.B: Tossing blood-stained gauze into the ordinary office waste bin
options.C: Recapping a needle carefully using both hands before disposal
